description: We are a team of six passionate learners participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in space exploration, science, research, and creative storytelling. Through this challenge, we aim to explore the stories behind NASA's past missions and bring forgotten space equipment and their legacies to life through an engaging digital experience. We value teamwork, curiosity, creativity, and learning together!
summary:
AFTERGLOW is an interactive storytelling website that explores four human-made artefacts left behind on the Moon and Mars: the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector Arrays, Sojourner, and Opportunity.

Each artefact tells a different story of exploration, engineering, scientific discovery, and legacy. Through visual storytelling, timelines, illustrations, and interactive explanations, AFTERGLOW helps visitors understand what these objects were designed to do, what they achieved, and why they remain on other worlds.

The project addresses a simple question: what happens to the things we leave behind when a space mission ends? By connecting historical missions with their continuing scientific significance, AFTERGLOW makes planetary exploration more accessible and encourages curiosity about the lasting impact of human exploration beyond Earth.
details:
AFTERGLOW is an interactive educational website designed to preserve and communicate the stories of human-made exploration artefacts that remain on the Moon and Mars.

The website is organised into four chapters, each focusing on a significant artefact: the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector Arrays, Sojourner, and Opportunity. Visitors can explore the purpose, engineering, operation, scientific contributions, and legacy of each artefact through structured storytelling, visual explanations, timelines, and interactive website elements.

The project aims to make space exploration history and planetary science easier to understand and more engaging for a general audience. It connects past missions with the scientific knowledge they continue to provide, demonstrating that the end of a mission does not necessarily mean the end of its contribution.

AFTERGLOW was developed as a web-based project using Google AI Studio, with AI assistance for website development. Research was guided by official NASA, NASA/JPL, NSSDC, and lunar laser ranging resources. NASA imagery and datasets were used as references for the historical and scientific content.

The creative approach behind AFTERGLOW is to tell the stories through the objects themselves rather than presenting four disconnected mission summaries. We considered factual accuracy, reliable sources, clarity of explanations, visual consistency, and accessibility for visitors who may have little prior knowledge of space science.

The intended impact is to encourage curiosity about planetary exploration, demonstrate the lasting value of scientific missions, and help visitors appreciate the stories and discoveries that remain long after spacecraft and their missions have gone silent.

Generative AI tools were used to assist with website code generation, research organisation, content drafting and presentation design. All factual content was reviewed against the cited sources, and external imagery and resources are acknowledged.
